messages:
olivia: Hey folks, first-day laptop snag. Ran Kandji enrollment on my M2 Max and SSH keys I used on my personal laptop won't load into the macOS Keychain. `ssh-add -l` shows nothing and Terminal keeps prompting for the old key passphrase. Need to push a new SSH cert from the CA or migrate keys. Who handles SSH certs and can grant a short temp-admin if needed?
onboard-bot: Welcome to Redwood, @olivia! :tada: IT handles device/keychain migrations and SSH cert onboarding. Pinging them now.
it-support: Hi Olivia  welcome! Quick checks: what does `security list-keychains` show and can you paste `ssh-add -l` and the output of `sw_vers -productVersion`? Did you restore from a Time Machine/Migration Assistant restore?
olivia: Running those now: 
`$ security list-keychains`
`"/Users/olivia/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db"`
`$ ssh-add -l`
`The agent has no identities.`
`$ sw_vers -productVersion`
`13.6.4`
I did migrate from my old personal Mac using Migration Assistant.
devops: Migration Assistant often pulls an old ssh-agent/keychain pairing that doesn't match the new login password, or it leaves keys in the user keychain but not unlocked by the agent. Two paths: (A) we migrate your private keys into the new login.keychain and add them to the agent (`ssh-add -K /path/to/id_rsa`) under temp-admin, or (B) issue a short-lived SSH certificate (preferred) via our CA tooling and install the CA public key on your Git hosts so you can authenticate without moving your private key.
security-bot: For security, we prefer certificates (option B). Certs expire quickly and avoid storing long-lived private keys in backups. But onboarding scripts that mint certs require the `redwood-ssh-renewer` helper to be installed (needs admin to place a LaunchDaemon). We can push it via Kandji or grant temp-admin for a supervised install.
it-support: If you want us to avoid manual sudo, we can push the renewer via Kandji policy. It will install under `/Library/LaunchDaemons` and set proper permissions. Policy check usually runs within 10 minutes. If you need immediate access for pairing to a sprint, I can grant a 30-minute temp-admin so you can run `ssh-add -K ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` and/or let us install the renewer. Which do you prefer?
olivia: If the cert route is faster overall I'm happy to wait for Kandji to push. But I do need git access for day-one tasks. How long does the cert issuance take after the helper is installed?
devops: Once `redwood-ssh-renewer` is installed and you authenticate via SSO, minting a certificate is seconds. I'll queue the Kandji install now for your serial.
people-ops: Welcome aboard @olivia :wave: If this blocks any onboarding steps we can mark them rescoped until IT confirms.
it-support: Pushed candji policy for `redwood-ssh-renewer` (target: your serial). Also temporarily opened a 30-minute admin window as backup; you'll receive a Kandji notification with the temp-admin token. Use it only if the renewer doesn't land within ~8 minutes.
olivia: Got the Kandji prompt and the temp-admin token. Renewer popped in and asked me to authenticate via the browser SSO flow. After SSO it minted a cert and `ssh -T git@github.com` worked immediately. I removed the private key from login keychain to avoid duplication.
security-bot: Verified certificate issued and logged. Noted that the renewer installed with expected LaunchDaemon flags. Good to rotate in ~7 days as per onboarding policy.
it-support: Closing the loop. If you prefer we can also migrate older keys to a secure company storage; DM us. Welcome to Redwood and enjoy your first day! :tada:
